text: Dr. Rosa tipped the big chair back, and a bright little light shone down like a tiny sun. "Open wide like a hippo," she said, counting teeth with a small silver mirror. Pip opened wide too, and a golden sparkle popped right out.

Nurse Ben held up the shot with its tiny needle. "This medicine teaches your body to fight off germs," he said. "It feels like a quick pinch." Maya squeezed Daddy's hand and blew out a slow breath, like cooling hot soup.

Dr. Amani warmed the stethoscope in her hands before pressing it to Maya's chest. Thump-thump, thump-thump. "Strong, happy heart," she said. Then she tapped Maya's knee with a tiny rubber hammer, and Maya's foot kicked all by itself!

Maya had a stuffy nose and a little fever, so she stayed home in her pajamas. Mommy brought tissues, a cool washcloth, and a bowl of chicken soup. "Ah-CHOO!" went Maya. "Ah-choo!" went Pip, sneezing a whole shower of golden sparkles.

At the hospital, Maya wore a gown covered in little moons. Dr. Lee showed her the sleepy mask. "It smells like strawberries," he said. "You'll nap while we take out your tonsils, and Mommy will be right here when you wake up."

That night, thunder rumbled outside the hospital window. Maya's throat was still sore from the operation, and Pip hiccupped a nervous sparkle. Maya pressed the call button, and Nurse Jo came with a cherry ice pop and an extra blanket.

Maya slid her new purple glasses onto her nose and gasped. On Moonberry Hill, every single leaf looked sharp and clear! "What if kids think they look funny?" she whispered. "Then they'll see how sparkly you look," said Pip, hiccupping just one.

Maya's scooter wobbled on the bumpy path, and down she went. Her knee was scraped and bleeding a little, and it stung. Daddy rinsed it with cool water while Maya took three slow breaths. Then he added a bandage covered in tiny blue dragons.
Mommy measured pink medicine into a tiny cup, right to the line. "Only take medicine when a grown-up gives it to you," she said. Maya gulped it down. Cherries, and a teeny bit like socks!

Grandpa lit a small fire in the fireplace and closed the safety screen. The flames crackled orange and gold while sniffly Maya snuggled under a quilt with warm honey-lemon tea. "Fire is for grown-ups to tend," Grandpa said. "We just get to enjoy the cozy."

Back in the Pillow Fort, Maya patted her brave-day sticker and yawned. Pip curled up on her pillow, warm as a mug of cocoa. "Doctors help us get better," Maya whispered. Her eyes grew heavy, and the night got soft and quiet.
Maya got two shots at her checkup today and she cried when the needle went in, but she held my hand and was really brave. Can you tell her a story about that?
Maya is having her tonsils taken out at the hospital on Friday and she's nervous about the operation and staying overnight. Tell her a calm bedtime story about it.
Maya's home with a bad cold and a fever and she keeps spitting out her medicine. Can the story help her feel okay about taking it tonight?
